title.narrative: GEF-8 Gouvernance intégrée et transformation urbaine pour un GLBV durable

description.narrative: The prevalent urban development model of the Grand Libreville, which hosts nearly 50% of Gabon’s population, is resulting in the loss, fragmentation and degradation of ecosystems of local, national and global significance,contributing to greenhouse gas emissions, increasing the vulnerability to climate change of local populations and generating growing inequalities. This unsustainable dynamic is due to fragmented and weak governance and regulatory frameworks for integrated urban planning, limited integration of nature-positive approaches in urban planning and development, insufficient mainstreaming of resilience and low carbon approaches in sectoral development, meagre financial resources at the municipal level, inadequate economic incentives for sustainable urban development, and limited technical capacities on and social awareness of the concepts and practices of sustainable urban development. The project catalyzes a paradigm shift by strengthening the governance and regulatory frameworks and increasing investments into urban sustainability (Component 1), upscaling nature positive and climate resilient interventions (Component 2), strengthening the contribution of sectoral investments in mobility, construction and waste to sustainable urban development (Component 3), and improving knowledge management, capacity building and communication (Component 4), with the support of robust M&E systems and processes (Component 5).

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
